sources.title: Gareth O. Roberts and Jeffrey S. Rosenthal, General State Space Markov Chains and MCMC Algorithms
sources.locator: Probability Surveys 1 (2004), Section 2, Definition and Proposition 1, PDF pp. 4–5.

contents.name: MCMC target stationarity equation (4)
contents.reason: The paper formulates invariance as integrating the transition kernel against the target law; the local proof identifies the two marginals of the joint flow measure for an arbitrary measurable space.

contents.name: Reversibility definition and Proposition 1 (reversibility implies stationarity)
contents.reason: The source states reversibility by symmetry of pi(dx)P(x,dy) and derives stationarity. The local definition makes the joint measure and coordinate transpose explicit, and the local theorem supplies the full measure-level marginal argument.

contents.name: Metropolis–Hastings construction and Proposition 2
contents.reason: Metropolis–Hastings construction belongs to the later BCS-30 pair; this page only establishes general reversibility and invariance.

sources.title: Sean P. Meyn and Richard L. Tweedie, Markov Chains and Stochastic Stability (1993), Chapter 10
sources.locator: §10.1.1, Invariant measures, equations (10.3)–(10.5), printed pp. 235–237; complete 26-page Chapter 10 PDF retrieved.

contents.name: Invariant probability equation (10.3) and iteration (10.4)
contents.reason: The chapter gives the general kernel identity pi(A)=integral pi(dx)P(x,A) and its iteration. The local result proves this identity from symmetric flow and does not claim the later stationary-process or convergence conclusions.

contents.name: Theorem 10.0.1: recurrence and uniqueness up to scale of an invariant measure
contents.reason: Existence and uniqueness from recurrence are not consequences of reversibility alone and are outside BCS-29.

contents.name: Proposition 10.1.1: positive chains are recurrent
contents.reason: The current pair adds no recurrence or irreducibility hypothesis and proves no recurrence result.

contents.name: Subinvariant-measure criteria in equations (10.6)–(10.10)
contents.reason: Subinvariance and recurrence criteria are not used by the general detailed-balance argument.
